All data work uses `data.table`, all graphics use `ggplot2`, and every plot is interactive through `ggiraph` (hover for tooltips and highlighting, use the toolbar to save a PNG) under one shared economic plot theme. Poverty lines are in 2021 PPP dollars per person per day: $3.00 (extreme poverty), $4.20 (lower-middle-income line) and $8.30 (upper-middle-income line). The poverty measures belong to the Foster--Greer--Thorbecke family: $$P_\alpha = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{q}\left(\frac{z-y_i}{z}\right)^{\alpha}$$ where $z$ is the poverty line, $y_i$ is income or consumption of poor person $i$, $q$ is the number of poor and $N$ the population. $\alpha=0$ gives the headcount ratio and $\alpha=1$ the poverty gap. Further measures used below: $$\text{Depth}=\frac{P_1}{P_0},\qquad \text{Palma}=\frac{S_{\text{top }10\%}}{S_{\text{bottom }40\%}},\qquad \text{Premium}=g_{\text{bottom }40}-g_{\text{mean}}$$ The Gini index is $G=\sum_i\sum_j |y_i-y_j| / (2n^2\bar y)$. A positive shared-prosperity premium means the bottom 40% grew faster than the average. Survey data are irregular, so cross-country comparisons use each country's **latest observation since 2015**. No population weights are in the file, so group averages across countries are unweighted medians; the World, region and income-group poverty series are the World Bank's population-weighted aggregates.
